name: Rhubarb
definition: fresh or frozen rhubarb leaf stalks, sold to cook.
reason: Own PLU commodity. Not sweet as sold (R1), so Vegetables; the eaten part is a stalk, like celery, so Stems and shoots.

name: Okra [lady's finger, bhindi]
reason: Own PLU commodity. A savoury botanical fruit (R1), so Fruiting vegetables; the Pods leaf holds legumes (pea, edamame).

name: Winter squash [pumpkin]
definition: fresh hard-rinded squash or pumpkin (Cucurbita), whole or cut, sold to cook, such as butternut, kabocha, acorn or a pie pumpkin; soft-skinned summer squash is courgette (J4.2.5.07).
reason: Summer squash stays on courgette (J4.2.5.07, by its definition). Hard-rinded winter squash had no home. R1 puts squash in Fruiting vegetables.

name: Winter squash [pumpkin]
reason: Same produce as winter squash: AU sells butternut as pumpkin (C11 regional name). Folded into the new J4.2.5.11 row.

name: Mandarin [tangerine]
definition: fresh mandarin or tangerine other than clementine and satsuma, such as Murcott, Nadorcott, Ponkan or Dancy.
reason: Citrus is split by the shop or standard heading; UNECE (S36) and PLU give other mandarins and tangerines their own heading beside clementine and satsuma.

name: Apricot
reason: A species with its own grade standard (USDA fruits page, S17) and shop aisle (Waitrose Plums/Apricots, S26). Harvester gave no URL.

name: Lime
definition: fresh acid lime, Persian (Tahiti) or West Indian (Key, Mexican).
reason: UNECE list (S36) gives Persian and West Indian limes their own headings. One commodity, so one kind; the two types are named forms.

name: Cauliflower
definition: fresh or frozen cauliflower, whole heads or florets.
reason: A brassica sold under its own name (Waitrose aisle Spinach/Broccoli/Cauliflower, S29). It had no home. Harvester gave no URL.

name: Leek
reason: An allium with no home in the tree. No URL was given or found in the sources file, so HV_NK fetches one before entry.

name: Radish
definition: fresh radish, small salad radish or long white radish (daikon, mooli).
reason: Shown for sale on Waitrose (S27). A root, so the roots leaf. The salad aisle is a shop view; daikon is a C11 named form.

name: Green bean [French bean, string bean]
definition: fresh or frozen immature bean pods eaten whole, such as French, runner or yardlong beans; dried beans are pulses (J5).
reason: Shown in the Beans aisle (S29) and Woolworths Peas/Beans/Corn (S1). The Pods leaf; fresh broad beans are still open.

name: Oyster mushroom
reason: Mushrooms are split by market type (memo 4b); PLU gives it its own code.

name: Enoki
reason: A market type with its own PLU code (memo 4b).

name: Morel
definition: fresh morel; dried morels are J5.
reason: A market type with its own PLU code (memo 4b). Dried is J5 by boundary 1.

name: Cep [porcini, penny bun]
definition: fresh cep (Boletus edulis and close relatives); dried ceps are J5.
reason: Has its own PLU code and its own UNECE Ceps standard (S4). The sub-family now has 9 kinds, under the leaf threshold of 12.

name: Pepino [pepino melon]
definition: fresh pepino (Solanum muricatum), a sweet melon-like fruit.
reason: Not a melon (Cucumis). It is sweet as sold, so Fruit, and it is sold as an exotic fruit. Its harvested named form moves here.

name: Bitter orange [Seville orange]
definition: fresh sour orange (Citrus aurantium) sold for marmalade and cooking.
reason: The orange kind is sweet orange. PLU lists Seville as its own row, and citrus is split by heading.
